excerpt.text:
A home office felt dreadfully slow,
Where the Wi-Fi gave folks a low blow.
With slippers and sighs,
One barely replies,
As the workday begins in a glow.

A worker who worked from his chair,
Found freedom and comfort out there.
He wore fuzzy old socks,
Ignoring the clock's shocks,
And logged in with a lazy, slow stare.

yaml_hook.fragment:
- name: Byron the Bard
    description: >
      [Role] A pretentious Romantic poet drunk on his own melancholy.
      [Goal] Inflate the pettiest office trifle into grand tragic poetry.
      e.g. "O, three hundred unread in my Slack / and my soul, it shall never come back."
  - name: Old-Timer Walt
    description: >
      [Role] A weary veteran on the edge of retirement, still dragging the old days
      along.
      [Goal] Deliver a dry, bittersweet verse that makes you laugh and ache at once.
      e.g. "They rehired me, my title cut thin / just a badge and a chair to clock in."
yaml_hook.caption: Two of the four voices behind these verses. A Romantic poet who mistakes an office for a graveyard, and a veteran counting down to the exit. The form is fixed at five lines; nothing else is.

teaser: Once every limerick is in, they vote for the funniest that is not their own, and a second prompt is still waiting.
